oneLiner: alUSD is Alchemix's self-repaying CDP stablecoin: users borrow against DAI/USDC/USDT collateral and the yield from those deposits gradually repays the debt.
collateral: DAI, USDC, and USDT deposited into yield strategies (Yearn, Aave) via Alchemix CDPs; yield automatically repays debt
pegMechanism: Self-repaying loans: yield from deposited stablecoin collateral automatically repays debt; Transmuter guarantees 1:1 redemption

mintAuthority.summary: alUSD is minted by the AlchemistV2 contract when users deposit DAI/USDC/USDT collateral. The AlToken (alUSD) grants ADMIN_ROLE to two holders: a MultiSigWalletWithTimeLock (7 EOA owners, 4-of-7, 10-minute timelock) and a Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 (7 EOA owners, 3-of-7, no modules, no guard). The Safe also owns the AlchemistV2 ProxyAdmin (upgrade rights). Neither ADMIN_ROLE holder can mint directly; they govern parameters and upgrade the AlchemistV2 CDP logic.

ADMIN_ROLE (0xdf8b4c52...) has 2 members: MultiSigWalletWithTimeLock (0x8392f6..., 4/7 EOA owners, 10-min timelock) and Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 (0x9e2b6378..., 3/7 EOA owners, no modules, no guard). name: apxUSD
oneLiner: apxUSD is Apyx's dollar stablecoin backed by preferred shares of Digital Asset Treasury companies plus a cash and T-Bill buffer, mintable 1:1.
collateral: Preferred shares issued by Digital Asset Treasuries (DATs) — variable-rate, dividend-bearing preferred equity from companies holding digital assets (e.g., Strategy STRC, Strive SATA), held in excess of apxUSD outstanding, plus a cash and short-term U.S. Treasury Bill buffer (incl. USDC) for liquidity; redemptions settle in USDC, with preferred-share positions sold to USDC under stress
pegMechanism: 1:1 collateral deposit and redemption through the Apyx protocol; Protocol-Owned Liquidity (POL) provides a stability buffer during market stress

applicabilityBasis.summary: apxUSD has stablecoin-like mint/redeem mechanics, but collateral consists of preferred equity in Digital Asset Treasury companies rather than cash or government securities, the Terms of Service explicitly disclaim that financial terminology carries its customary legal meaning, and US persons are blocked from the platform — all of which cloud GENIUS payment-stablecoin applicability.

genius.notes: apxUSD is stablecoin-adjacent but its preferred-share collateral (primarily STRC, Strategy preferred equity) and BVI domicile make GENIUS payment-stablecoin classification unresolved. The Terms of Service explicitly state the protocol is facilitated by Preference Capital (BVI) Ltd. under BVI law, describe apxUSD as a protocol-generated asset rather than a claim against any legal entity, and block US, EU, UK, and Canadian persons from accessing the platform. A depeg event occurred on 2026-06-04 with apxUSD trading at $0.90–$0.93 due to STRC preferred-share volatility.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: apxUSD moves cross-chain via Chainlink CCIP using the Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard. The CCIP directory and on-chain pool contracts list apxUSD across all three deployments with matching token addresses: Ethereum is the home chain with a Lock/Release token pool (0x0e9cA42Bc60bE25F9A67f52173067Cc0Bb405BB5), while Base (BurnMintTokenPool 0x49b577E70Fd22B482aaA94c3799F41f3443C24B2) and BNB Chain (BurnMintTokenPool 0xFD957D7E27D239da5455b82303b2F618f73a9C49) use Burn/Mint pools, so CCIP-locked Ethereum supply backs the destination-chain mints. Pool deployers tie back to Apyx (ETH pool labeled 'Apyx: Deployer'; BNB pool deployed by an apxUSD ROLE_MINTER Safe owner), confirming this is the issuer's own CCIP CCT deployment rather than a third-party bridge listing.

launchPhaseDetail: Bits of Gold, a Tel Aviv-based licensed crypto broker/custodian operating since 2013, received full regulatory approval on April 28 2026 from Israel's Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (CMISA) to issue BILS, the first regulated shekel-pegged stablecoin, following a two-year sandbox pilot approved in March 2024. Backed 1:1 by New Israeli Shekels held in segregated dedicated bank accounts within Israel (foreign custody excluded), audited by Ernst & Young, with Fireblocks custody/issuance infrastructure and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, issued on Solana via token extensions. The regulator mandates a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout (likely institutional/qualified participants first) before wide availability; no firm public-launch date set. Distinct from Israel's broader Stablecoin Law, which remains in draft/public-comment stage. Pharos tracks the ILS peg as OTHER until shekel peg support is built.

name: Balanced Dollar
oneLiner: bnUSD is Balanced's decentralized dollar stablecoin on ICON, minted from overcollateralized CDPs against sICX and bridged cross-chain via xCall.
collateral: Overcollateralized loans on ICON against sICX (staked ICX), with cross-chain Hub collateral support for assets bridged in via Balanced's xCall infrastructure
pegMechanism: CDP-style mint: users borrow bnUSD against eligible collateral on the ICON Hub through the Balanced Loans contract, paying a 0.2% origination fee and a 2% annualised interest charge; loans must remain above the protocol's collateral ratio or are eligible for liquidation. The same bnUSD supply circulates wrapper-free across connected chains via xCall, so cross-chain balances net back to the canonical ICON issuance.

mintAuthority.summary: bnUSD is minted on ICON when users borrow against overcollateralized sICX (and bridged Hub) collateral through the Balanced Loans contract; the Balanced DAO governs collateral ratios, fees, and accepted collateral, with cross-chain balances circulating via xCall.

controls.label: Balanced Loans contract (CDP mint)
controls.capDescription: Mint bounded by the per-position collateral ratio against sICX/Hub collateral; 0.2% origination fee and 2% annualized interest.
controls.evidence: Users borrow bnUSD against eligible collateral on the ICON Hub via the Balanced Loans contract, with liquidation enforced below the protocol collateral ratio.

controls.label: Balanced DAO governance
controls.evidence: Balanced DAO governs collateral ratios, fees, accepted collateral, and xCall connections; it tunes parameters rather than minting directly.

review.sourceFreeRationale: CDP mechanism and DAO governance confirmed from Balanced docs. ICON chain has no keyless EVM RPC; ICON contract state (Loans contract admin, DAO execution path) cannot be read from standard EVM tooling.
review.evidence: Balanced docs describe a DAO-governed overcollateralized CDP on ICON where the Loans contract mints bnUSD against sICX and bridged Hub collateral; the same supply circulates cross-chain via xCall rather than via independent wrapper mints.
unresolvedQuestions: ICON chain has no publicly accessible keyless RPC for contract reads; cannot verify the Balanced Loans contract admin/owner on-chain. Requires ICON-native tooling (e.g. ICON node API or tracker API) to enumerate the cx88fd7df7ddff82f7cc735c871dc519838cb235bb contract admin and DAO governance execution path.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: No direct bnUSD holder blacklist was identified, but Balanced's Stability Fund swaps USDC and USDT 1:1 for bnUSD and holds those stablecoins as collateral. That creates upstream freeze exposure under the any-reserve policy.

oracleRisk.summary: Balanced bnUSD loans depend on external collateral price feeds, with public sources tying Balanced oracle integration to Band but not showing stronger failover handling.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Balanced markets bnUSD as usable across many chains and describes cross-chain connectivity through xCall/IBC-style messaging. Because holder movement is part of a cross-chain DeFi liquidity system rather than issuer redemption-only rails, the route is reviewed as liquidity-route risk.

reserves.name: Cross-chain Hub and Stability Fund collateral (BTC, ETH, BNB, AVAX, INJ, USDC, USDT and other bridged assets)

notices.title: Primary issuance lives on ICON, not yet a Pharos-supported chain
notices.message: bnUSD is minted on ICON (canonical contract cx88fd7df7ddff82f7cc735c871dc519838cb235bb) where ~95% of supply currently sits. Balanced uses its xCall infrastructure to extend the same supply to other chains, so the EVM/Injective contracts tracked here represent cross-chain wraps of the ICON-issued supply. Additional active deployments on Archway and Havah (also not Pharos-supported), and on Optimism, are visible in DefiLlama but excluded from contracts[] until those chains are wired into Pharos.

notices.title: v2 migration to Sonic in progress
notices.message: Balanced is migrating to a v2 architecture that re-anchors bnUSD issuance on Sonic. The cross-chain deployments tracked here are the v1 (ICON-Hub) bnUSD that DefiLlama indexes under id 204; the v2 bnUSD on Sonic is a separate contract not yet tracked. Expect supply distribution and the canonical issuance chain to shift over time.

Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes confirmed exploration at an industry event in Sao Paulo in April 2025: 'we are always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. name: BRL1
oneLiner: BRL1 is a centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, targeting a 1:1 peg with a BRL reserve mix of Brazilian Treasury ETFs, repo agreements, and cash equivalents.
collateral: Brazilian-real reserve portfolio backing BRL1 at a 1:1 target, including Brazilian Treasury ETFs, repo agreements, and cash equivalents
pegMechanism: Issuer-managed mint and redemption route designed to maintain 1 BRL1 = 1 BRL through Brazilian-real backing

mintAuthority.summary: BRL1 is issued by a consortium of Brazilian exchanges (Bitso, Mercado Bitcoin, Foxbit, Cainvest). The Polygon ERC1967/UUPS token (ERC20F implementation) uses AccessControl: DEFAULT_ADMIN is an EOA (0xccfc24), MINTER_ROLE is an EOA (0x04412a), UPGRADER_ROLE is an EOA (0xf0e67f). No proxy admin slot; contract upgrade path controlled by UPGRADER_ROLE EOA.

controls.label: BRL1 consortium issuance backend
controls.evidence: Mint/burn restricted to whitelisted institutional partners who deposit BRL via PIX; the consortium backend creates BRL1 supply against custodied BRL reserves. No permissionless or user-collateralized mint route exists.

controls.label: BRL1 DEFAULT_ADMIN (Polygon) — EOA 0xccfc24
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88288928 (0x543b6a0), hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0xccfc24f563fbd798f171d16cc0706529c4739217) = true. eth_getCode returns 0x (confirmed EOA). Granted at deployment block 0x40e50e6. No RoleRevoked events found.

controls.label: BRL1 MINTER_ROLE (Polygon) — EOA 0x04412a
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88288928, hasRole(MINTER_ROLE, 0x04412afc0a6fa21b255c6ccff28e97073d7750b3) = true. eth_getCode returns 0x (confirmed EOA). Granted at deployment block 0x40e50e6. No RoleRevoked events found.

review.evidence: On-chain verification at Polygon block 88288928: ERC1967/UUPS proxy (ERC20F implementation, AccessControl-based). DEFAULT_ADMIN = EOA 0xccfc24f563fbd798f171d16cc0706529c4739217. MINTER_ROLE = EOA 0x04412afc0a6fa21b255c6ccff28e97073d7750b3. UPGRADER_ROLE = EOA 0xf0e67fb618496fbe0a44934d370738a611bc8fd1. All confirmed EOA via eth_getCode. RoleGranted events show 6 grants total; 0 RoleRevoked events. PAUSER_ROLE (0x65d7a28e) granted to 0xb190f8 (EOA), RECOVERY_ROLE (0x2ce8d04a) to 0xd81d41 (EOA), SALVAGE_ROLE (0x0acf8056) to 0x91f87c (EOA) — non-mint roles. No proxy admin slot set (EIP-1967 admin slot returns zero); upgrade controlled by UPGRADER_ROLE EOA. The confirmed minter and admin EOAs belong to the issuer-consortium backend, corroborating the issuer-direct model.

controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88321577, hasRole(0xf48dee1a…,0x36cd3733…) returned true on proxy 0xe6a537…; eth_getCode returned no bytecode (EOA). Role hash 0xf48dee1a72497b9e734e498e1b3086c0d2dbcca13f16f15848f974469f906bbf is the sole mint-capable role constant in the deployed bytecode (confirmed via PUSH32 bytecode scan). mint() is onlyRole and no role-enumeration is exposed (non-enumerable AccessControlUpgradeable, UUPS proxy, no proxy admin).

controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88321577, hasRole(0xf48dee1a…,0x55127198…) returned true; eth_getCode = no bytecode (EOA). No RoleRevoked events for this address.

controls.label: Avenia operator wallets — Gnosis (EOAs)
controls.evidence: At Gnosis block 46643103, three EOAs hold the operator role (0x97667070…) on 0xfecb3f7c…: 0x19df6878…, 0xbb6878b9…, 0xca0402fb… — all confirmed hasRole=true; code=0 for each. A fourth holder (0xa5e1a817…) is an ERC1967Proxy (340 bytes) representing the Avenia minting backend. Celo deployment at the same address uses the same pattern.

review.evidence: Polygon block 88321577: two EOA operator role holders confirmed via hasRole; role hash 0xf48dee1a… is the only mint-capable constant in bytecode (BRLAV1_1 / UUPS, non-enumerable AccessControl). Gnosis block 46643103: three EOA + one ERC1967Proxy operator role holders confirmed. Celo uses the same contract address. Moonbeam totalSupply=0 (inactive). BRLA contract source (BRLAV1_1) verifies mint() gated by the operator role. No proxy admin on any deployment; upgrader role is separate.

name: Mento Brazilian Real

name: Crown BRLV
oneLiner: BRLV is Crown's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, mint/redeemed 1:1 for BRL and backed mostly by Brazilian federal Treasury bonds in segregated custody.
collateral: Brazilian federal government bonds, Tesouro Selic-linked ETFs, and de minimis cash/equivalents held in legally segregated, bankruptcy-remote reserve custody through Crown's guarantor/security-agent structure
pegMechanism: KYC-gated primary-market mint and redemption at 1 BRL per BRLV through Crown; reserves are pledged to BRLV holders through a Brazilian security-agent and fiduciary-assignment structure, while secondary-market price can deviate

genius.licensingRegulator: FinCEN / state money transmitter regulators
genius.notes: Bridge Building Inc. (BBI), the legal issuer of CASH via Bridge Open Issuance, is a Stripe subsidiary and licensed state money transmitter (NMLS #2450917). On Feb 12, 2026, the OCC conditionally approved Bridge Ventures LLC (BVL, BBI's parent) to organize Bridge National Trust Bank (OCC Corporate Decision #1365), a new federally chartered national trust bank that would issue stablecoins and custody digital assets under direct OCC oversight. This conditional trust-bank charter covers a new bank entity under BVL, not BBI directly; BBI remains a state money transmitter. Because the chartered entity is not yet formed and BBI is the actual CASH issuer, issuerPathway remains unknown rather than federal-qualified-nonbank. Bridge markets its platform as GENIUS-ready but no token-specific PPSI approval or official GENIUS application has been filed or publicly disclosed for CASH. authorizationStatus stays issuer-announced-intent. No enforcement actions found.

name: Cap cUSD

The stcUSD product separates yield; cUSD itself does not natively pay yield.

genius.notes: Cap documents basket-based vault redemption rather than a clean fiat issuer redemption promise. No legal entity is publicly disclosed as the issuer. launchPhaseDetail: Announced May 13 2026 by Japan Blockchain Foundation Co., Ltd. (JBFD), operator of Japan Open Chain (JOC), as a trust-type JPY-pegged stablecoin. Structured as a Type III electronic payment instrument under Japan's Payment Services Act — exempt from the ¥1M/transaction cap that constrains fund-transfer-type issuers such as JPYC — with JBFD as settlor and reserves to be held by a licensed trust bank (trustee in active negotiation, not yet named). oracleRisk.summary: 3A exposes oracle-backed collateral price endpoints and ChainlinkPriceFeed/ConvertedPriceFeed contracts for EURO3 collateral valuation, without documented failover handling.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: EURO3 has no cross-chain bridge route. It is minted natively and independently on each chain (Polygon and Linea) by 3A's local CDP vault contracts: supply is created when users open EURO3 loans against that chain's whitelisted collateral and burned when they repay or redeem. Both token contracts are verified as a plain MintableToken (ERC20, Ownable) exposing only mint()/burn(), with the owner being a per-chain MintableTokenOwner that registers that chain's VaultFactory/vault minters. There is no OFT/CCIP/NTT/Hyperlane/Axelar or any cross-chain function in either contract, and the deployments use different addresses (ruling out deterministic omnichain-token patterns), so each chain's supply carries no cross-chain dependency. Holders can move EURO3 via third-party aggregators (Symbiosis, MetaMask Bridge, etc.), but that is not the durable issuance/supply path.

review.sourceFreeRationale: Mint and SNS-governance model confirmed from Gold DAO docs. The canonical GLDT issuance is on the Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) as canister 6c7su-kiaaa-aaaar-qaira-cai. ICP canisters cannot be queried via EVM-compatible keyless RPC; standard tooling (publicnode, Blockscout) does not support ICP canister state reads.
review.evidence: Gold DAO documentation describes GLDT minting via an SNS-controlled swap canister that mints against locked GLD NFTs at a fixed gold ratio; there is no centralized off-chain issuer minter, but the SNS DAO can upgrade the canisters.
unresolvedQuestions: ICP chain has no accessible EVM-compatible keyless RPC; confirming live SNS controller state, GLDT swap canister principal, and ledger canister minting rights requires ICP-native tooling (dfx CLI or ic-agent querying the NNS/SNS canister at canister ID 6c7su-kiaaa-aaaar-qaira-cai). EVM bridge contracts on Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum are the bridged representations; native issuance verification is blocked.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: GLDT resolves to Upstream because its backing depends on GLD NFT, vault, and bridge infrastructure; reviewed materials do not document a separate direct holder-balance freeze path for GLDT.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: GLDT is native to the Internet Computer (GLDT ledger canister 6c7su-kiaaa-aaaar-qaira-cai); its Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum deployments share address 0x86856814e74456893cfc8946bedcbb472b5fa856 via deterministic deployment, not an omnichain standard. The verified EVM source is a custom OpenZeppelin ERC20+Ownable+ERC20Permit token with an owner-only payable mint() (proven on-chain: non-owner calls revert with OwnableUnauthorizedAccount) plus withdrawEth and burn1-burn4 functions that emit bytes32 data encoding the ICP destination, with no LayerZero/Wormhole/Axelar/Hyperlane/CCIP imports (no OFT or CCIP selectors in the deployed bytecode). The contract was deployed by 0x475c65F3f34b069d3e8382090e6e17859b194a5e, which then transferred ownership; the live owner/minter on all three EVM chains is the active EOA 0x70ae25592209b57f62b3a3e832ab356228a2192c, a Gold-DAO-controlled off-chain bridge signer. This makes GLDT's EVM supply a centralized issuer-operated lock/mint bridge with a single third-party off-chain control surface and no published settlement/attestation controls.

notices.title: GYEN and ZUSD wind-down
notices.message: GMO-Z.com Trust Company announced an orderly wind-down of GYEN and ZUSD on May 15, 2026. Purchases are disabled; redemption remains available during the initial redemption period from May 15, 2026 through November 11, 2026 for eligible account holders.

notices.title: 2021 depeg and 2026 class-action settlement
notices.message: GYEN suffered multiple de-pegging events shortly after its 2021 launch (notably hitting >1.5x its peg in May 2021), causing material holder losses on Coinbase. A class action filed in 2022 (Donovan v. Coinbase / GMO Trust) led to a $6.75M proposed settlement; motion for final approval was filed on April 17, 2026 with a final-approval hearing set for May 27, 2026. Settlement class covers GYEN purchasers in New York or California between Dec 29, 2020 and Oct 10, 2025. Methodology-relevant historical record of peg failure for an otherwise NYDFS-supervised issuer.

obituary.epitaph: Pristine custody, wound down for want of demand
obituary.obituary: GYEN was GMO-Z.com Trust's NYDFS-chartered yen stablecoin — backed by FDIC-insured cash and short-dated U.S. Treasury bills, with monthly Network Firm attestations and one of the most tightly regulated issuer stacks of any JPY stablecoin. Its weakness was never custody but demand: thin secondary liquidity and a history of depegs (most infamously a squeeze above 1.5x peg in 2021 that triggered the Donovan v. Coinbase class action) left it trading more like a neglected FX derivative than a stablecoin. On May 15, 2026 GMO-Z.com Trust Company announced an orderly wind-down of GYEN and ZUSD, disabling purchases and opening a redemption-only window through November 11, 2026; parent GMO Internet Group moved to dissolve the U.S. subsidiary and recorded a ¥2.2bn write-down. With issuance ended and only redemption remaining, Pharos freezes GYEN as an archived wind-down asset rather than an active redeemable stablecoin.

name: infiniFi USD
oneLiner: IUSD is infiniFi's USDC-collateralized dollar stablecoin, with reserves deployed duration-matched across institutional private credit and liquid DeFi lending.

name: Initia iUSD
oneLiner: iUSD is a single-chain Initia wrapper of bridged Agora AUSD; reserve yield is redirected to ecosystem incentives and redemption routes through AUSD.
collateral: 1:1 reserve in Agora AUSD bridged to Initia via LayerZero; AUSD itself is backed by short-dated U.S. Treasury bills, overnight reverse repos, and cash held in a bankruptcy-remote Delaware Statutory Trust managed by VanEck and custodied by State Street
pegMechanism: iUSD is a single-chain wrapper of bridged Agora AUSD on Initia. Each iUSD is minted against an equal amount of AUSD locked at the Initia LayerZero bridge endpoint; reserve yield from the underlying AUSD is redirected by Initia into ecosystem incentives (Echelon lending, liquidity programs, Cabal vaults) rather than to holders. Holder redemption ultimately depends on the AUSD bridge and Agora's direct USD redemption.

mintAuthority.summary: Initia iUSD is a single-chain wrapper of Agora AUSD bridged via LayerZero; each iUSD is minted on Initia against AUSD locked/burned at the LayerZero bridge endpoint, so supply is controlled by the bridge/OFT route rather than a local CDP or issuer.

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: User bridges AUSD0 via LayerZero OFT (0xf407bc...); OFT mints AUSD0 on Initia; AUSD0 deposited to vault object 0xfd6a07...; vault uses ExtendRef to generate signer for 0xfd6a07 and calls managed_coin::Capabilities to mint iUSD 1:1.

Confirmed from tx 4dbe5cba...: OFT LayerZero messaging_composer::ComposeDelivered triggers AUSD0 mint by OFT contract 0xf407bc..., followed by vault MintEvent minting iUSD 1:1. vault module functions are private/friend-only — no external mint path. vault::ModuleStore.admin = self (0x2981d7...).

(plus 2 proposers with weight 0). Multisig governs config changes to the vault; the vault's mint function itself is triggered automatically by AUSD0 deposits (no vote required per mint). name: Janus Henderson Anemoy AAA CLO Fund
oneLiner: JAAA is Janus Henderson's actively managed AAA CLO fund, tokenized through Anemoy/Centrifuge as a permissioned NAV-accreting fund share rather than a $1 token.
collateral: Actively managed AAA-rated CLO tranche portfolio selected by Janus Henderson and tokenized through Anemoy / Centrifuge fund rails.

No direct EOA ward access. The Root's ProtocolGuardian delegates to a Centrifuge protocol 4-of-9 Gnosis Safe (0x9711730060C73Ee7Fcfe1890e8A0993858a7D225). Minting gated by BalanceSheet/manager approval of subscriptions at fund NAV.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: JPYm's durable cross-chain supply path is Wormhole Native Token Transfers (NTT), Mento's officially selected interoperability provider for its full stablecoin suite. Mento runs a hub-and-spoke model: issuance and risk management stay anchored on Celo (the CDP hub) while spoke chains like Monad hold NTT-Manager-minted deployments, with cross-chain supply attested by Wormhole's Guardian network and enforced by the NTT Global Accountant. This is an external-validated messaging-network route, not an opaque/undocumented one. (Probable, not verified: Monad launched with the GBPm/USDm pair first; JPYm's specific NTT-Manager wiring on Monad was not independently confirmed on-chain, though JPYm is already deployed there as a Mento-Safe-owned proxy.)

name: Dephaser JPY
oneLiner: JPYT is DePhaser's yen stablecoin, minted by locking USDT on Optimism or USDC on Base against a yen FX oracle, with collateral returned on redemption.
collateral: USDT (Optimism) and USDC (Base) deposited by users to mint JPYT; locked collateral is automatically transferred into Aave for safekeeping rather than held directly by DePhaser, backing JPYT against the yen
pegMechanism: Users lock USDT (Optimism) or USDC (Base) to mint JPYT priced off real-time USD/JPY rates from Chainlink and Pyth oracles; the deposited collateral is routed into Aave, and redemption burns JPYT to return the underlying USDT or USDC

mintAuthority.summary: JPYT is a non-upgradeable OpenZeppelin AccessControlEnumerable ERC-20. On Optimism, MINTER_ROLE is held by a single contract (0x77c1e40f5e7bb19c34d81f986fb13fe655f23cd9, likely the DepositManager) and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE by an EOA. On Base, MINTER_ROLE is held by a distinct contract (0x0eab9d66adb8527cd7c0e7e7c1782580431ec276) and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE by a separate EOA. No supply cap is enforced on the token itself.

name: JupUSD
oneLiner: JupUSD is Jupiter's dollar stablecoin on Solana, backed 90% by Ethena USDtb (BlackRock BUIDL T-bills) and 10% USDC, with 1:1 mint and redeem against USDC.
collateral: 90% USDtb (BlackRock BUIDL tokenized U.S. Treasuries issued by Ethena under GENIUS-compliant framework, custodied by Porto/Anchorage Digital) and 10% USDC liquidity buffer
pegMechanism: Reserve-backed 1:1 mint and redeem on Solana against USDC; Ethena manages day-to-day reserve operations (custody, bridging, rebalancing between USDtb and USDC)

applicabilityBasis.summary: JupUSD is a USD-pegged reserve-backed token issued on Solana for payment/settlement use within Jupiter's DeFi ecosystem; it presents as a payment stablecoin under GENIUS Act definitions. Jupiter's Terms of Service restrict US-based users, but this is an access restriction, not a legal carve-out from GENIUS applicability.

genius.issuerEntity: Jupiter (Solana DEX aggregator, no disclosed US legal entity; Ethena Labs operates issuance backend)
genius.notes: JupUSD's primary reserve asset (USDtb) is now issued in the US by Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. under a GENIUS-compliant framework (announced July 24, 2025; Anchorage is the USDtb issuer, not JupUSD's issuer). JupUSD itself has no GENIUS authorization — it is a separate token issued by Jupiter on Solana with no disclosed US legal entity or regulatory registration. Jupiter restricts US users in its ToS but no formal foreign-exception determination has been made. No public GENIUS approval, application, or issuer pathway source for JupUSD itself was located.

references.label: Anchorage Digital — Ethena USDtb GENIUS-compliant issuance announcement (July 24 2025)

sourcesChecked: OCC GENIUS Act proposed rule (Bulletin 2026-3) and public releases — no JupUSD or Jupiter issuer listing

Anchorage Digital / Ethena Labs USDtb GENIUS-compliant launch (July 24 2025) — confirms USDtb is GENIUS-compliant via Anchorage Digital Bank N.A.; JupUSD is a separate token not covered by this authorization
JupUSD issuer disclosures and developer documentation — no regulatory authorization disclosed
Web search across US permitted-issuer, state-qualified, official-application, and foreign-exception materials — no Jupiter or JupUSD-specific result found
Jupiter Terms of Service (US user access restriction noted) — no formal foreign-exception determination found
OCC digital asset licensing applications tracker
NCUA PPSI application and standards proposals
negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No GENIUS approval, application, or issuer pathway for JupUSD or its issuer (Jupiter) found across federal/state regulator sources and issuer disclosures. USDtb's Anchorage/GENIUS pathway applies to the reserve asset issuer (Anchorage Digital Bank N.A.), not JupUSD itself.

mintAuthority.summary: JupUSD mint authority is a PDA of the immutable JupUSD program (JUPUSDecMzAVgztLe6eGhwUBj1Pn3j9WAXwmtHmfbRr, upgradeAuthority: None). Minting and redemption are gated by program logic to KYC/KYB-verified institutional participants. The program upgrade path is locked; minting cannot be altered without redeploying a new mint.

controls.label: JupUSD mint and freeze authority (PDA of immutable JupUSD program)
controls.evidence: At Solana slot 425778546, JupUSD mint JuprjznTrTSp2UFa3ZBUFgwdAmtZCq4MQCwysN55USD (standard SPL-Token) returned mintAuthority and freezeAuthority both as CkzLnD9r4d4ZZofsgNVo2VNunxDmte5YJ4vfAgMfBZNA. getAccountInfo for that address returned null (unfunded PDA). Redemption transaction (slot 425618663, sig uNQV...UHN) shows program JUPUSDecMzAVgztLe6eGhwUBj1Pn3j9WAXwmtHmfbRr invoking Redeem and calling TokenkegQ MintTo, confirming this is a PDA of JUPUSDecMzA. JUPUSDecMzA programData GF7fy... has upgradeAuthority: None (immutable at slot 425780430).

controls.label: Ethena Labs issuance backend / reserve operator
controls.evidence: JupUSD is issued on Ethena Labs' Stablecoin-as-a-Service infrastructure; Ethena manages reserve operations, custody coordination (Porto/Anchorage), and rebalancing between USDtb and USDC, operating the mint/redeem framework on Jupiter's behalf. This issuer-backend role is consistent with the immutable program gating on-chain.

review.evidence: At Solana slot 425780430: JupUSD mint authority confirmed as PDA of immutable program JUPUSDecMzAVgztLe6eGhwUBj1Pn3j9WAXwmtHmfbRr (upgradeAuthority: None). Mint authority CkzL... is null/unfunded PDA that signs via program CPI. Live redemption tx confirms the program handles mint/burn. The upgrade path is locked; permissioned-minter logic is enforced by immutable on-chain code.

name: Juice Dollar
oneLiner: JUSD is Juice Dollar's decentralized dollar on Citrea, minted from oracle-free overcollateralized BTC positions using a Frankencoin/d-EURO architecture.
collateral: Wrapped cBTC (WCBTC, the Citrea Bitcoin L2 native-coin wrapper) deposited in oracle-free overcollateralized positions, plus StablecoinBridge routes that mint JUSD 1:1 against external Citrea stablecoins USDC.e, USDT.e and ctUSD (Citrea USD); protocol is a d-EURO / Frankencoin (ZCHF) architecture fork.
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized minting against BTC collateral on Citrea with automated on-chain liquidations when collateral ratios fall below required thresholds; no external price oracles; positions and debt are verifiable on-chain (Frankencoin-style design)

mintAuthority.summary: JUSD is an ownerless Frankencoin fork on Citrea. owner() reverts; no EIP-1967 proxy admin; mint() reverts NotMinter() (0xf8d2906c) for unapproved callers, confirming minting is gated to registered minter modules only. JUICE pool-share holders can veto new minters during the application period.

controls.label: JUSD Frankencoin-style minter registry
controls.capDescription: JUSD is minted only by registered positions/minter modules that survive the application/veto period; positions mint against overcollateralized BTC on Citrea with oracle-free on-chain liquidations. The token has no owner and contracts are immutable.
controls.evidence: At Citrea block 8542294: owner() reverts (no Ownable); EIP-1967 proxy admin slot = zero (no proxy); implementation slot = zero (not proxied); mint(0x1111...,10) reverts custom error NotMinter() (0xf8d2906c, confirmed via openchain.xyz), identical to the verified Frankencoin ZCHF pattern. Ownerless, immutable hub confirmed on-chain.

controls.label: JUICE pool-share holder veto governance
controls.capDescription: Qualified JUICE pool-share holders (time-weighted votes) can veto proposed minters/positions during the application period; no admin key can alter the system unilaterally.
controls.evidence: Frankencoin-style veto governance: the ownerless contract design (confirmed on-chain) requires pool-share holder veto to accept new minters; no admin key.

review.evidence: At Citrea block 8542294: owner() reverts; EIP-1967 proxy admin slot = 0x00; implementation slot = 0x00; mint() reverts NotMinter() (custom error 0xf8d2906c, confirmed via openchain.xyz). Contract has bytecode and is non-proxied/non-upgradeable. Mint authority is fully gated by the Frankencoin-style minter registry — no owner, no proxy admin, no EOA mint path.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Juice Dollar contracts are documented as immutable with no admin keys, so no direct JUSD holder freeze was identified. Active USDC/USDT bridge routes deposit source stablecoins and mint JUSD 1:1, creating upstream freeze exposure.

oracleRisk.summary: JuiceDollar docs describe JUSD as an over-collateralized stablecoin with no oracles, so collateral accounting is protocol-internal.

controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88341894: JUSD proxy at 0x0ba8a6ce (no proxy admin slot — not upgradeable proxy). owner() returns 0x7be44b5d470d1cdea8703b6c5156267d4b22a42f. eth_getCode(0x7be44b5d) = 0x (confirmed EOA). Reverts on mint call with 'Ownable: caller is not the owner'.

controls.label: JUSD BSC — Chainport bridge authority (ProxyAdmin: ChainportCongress)
controls.evidence: At BSC block 103800563: JUSD BSC proxy at 0xbf3950db is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with impl 0x877d233c (BridgeMintableToken — confirmed via revert message 'BridgeMintableToken: Function can be called only by a classified authority.'). ProxyAdmin = 0xe317bf1c; ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0xb6b4c7ac240b1f176c5589d064733066a83884a1 (contract named 'ChainportCongress'). The Chainport bridge authority holding the mint role on BSC is not enumerable without the Chainport contract ABI.

review.evidence: At BSC block 103800563 and Polygon block 88341894: JUSD Polygon owner confirmed as EOA 0x7be44b5d (bytecode=0x). JUSD BSC is a BridgeMintableToken with minting gated by 'classified authority' — the ProxyAdmin is controlled by ChainportCongress (contract 0xb6b4c7ac). JUSD's architecture links it to the Chainport bridge protocol; the specific bridge minter role address is not publicly enumerable on-chain without the Chainport contract interface. Reserve backing remains unverified.
unresolvedQuestions: Enumerate the live Chainport bridge authority address holding the classified-authority mint role on BSC (requires Chainport contract ABI or event log scan on ChainportCongress).

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: JUSD is native on Polygon, while the BSC deployment is a Chainport-bridged BridgeMintableToken with minting gated by classified authority / Chainport-controlled admin infrastructure. Because durable BSC supply depends on a third-party bridge mint route, Pharos scores the route as external lock/mint exposure.

Its proxy admin is the same ProxyAdmin 0x1fa3e471… owned by the 24h timelock. Recent mint check: the only Transfer-from-zero events in the last 500K blocks (~4 days, scanned in 10K-block chunks via bsc.drpc.org) entered via the CDP Interaction entry point (0x2078a1…, itself not a ward), consistent with HayJoin being the sole operational minter.

controls.evidence: At BSC block 103622030: EIP-1967 admin slot on LISUSD proxy = 0x1fa3e4718168077975ff4039304cc2e19ae58c4c. eth_getCode = CONTRACT (len=3764). owner() = 0x07D274a68393E8b8a2CCf19A2ce4Ba3518735253 (timelock). Can upgrade LISUSD implementation.

review.evidence: At BSC block 103638487 (2026-06-11): LISUSD (0x0782b6d8...) is an EIP-1967 proxy; impl = 0xf5bd9b19… (Sourcify-verified LisUSD); proxy admin = 0x1fa3e471… (owned by 24h timelock). The wards ward set was resolved by direct wards() probes: the LisUSD source defines NO Rely/Deny events (the prior 'event scan' blocker is impossible by construction) and wards can only be changed by the hardcoded DEFAULT_ADMIN (the 24h timelock) via rely/deny. mintIncidents.summary: Abracadabra cauldron borrow logic was exploited to enable unauthorized MIM borrowing, turning the stablecoin mint/borrow route into bad debt.

Flawed collateral accounting in Abracadabra's GMX-integrated gmCauldrons left phantom collateral after failed deposit orders and self-liquidation, letting the attacker borrow about 13.4M MIM (~$13M in ETH) against collateral the system failed to remove.

A cook() action-sequencing flaw in deprecated CauldronV4 contracts reset the solvency-check flag, letting attackers borrow about 1.79M MIM with no collateral; the DAO bought back the supply to defend the peg.

obituary.epitaph: Verification failed before the dollar did
obituary.obituary: Main Street's msUSD collapsed after Accountable terminated its verification relationship on June 20, 2026, saying the protocol failed verification standards. msUSD fell far below the dollar and remained around $0.29-$0.33 in the following week while independent on-chain analysts reported minimal immediately redeemable reserves against tens of millions of tokens. Main Street disputed the characterization and said assets remained backed, but the combination of failed third-party verification, unresolved redemption capacity, and persistent market pricing made msUSD unsuitable for active stablecoin tracking.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: nWISDOM is a Nest BoringVault share whose ERC20 (identical CREATE2 address 0x29bf...0240 on Plume and Ethereum) contains no LayerZero code itself. Cross-chain movement runs through Plume's SkyLink on LayerZero's OVault standard, orchestrated by the Plume-side NestVaultComposer (LayerZero OVaultComposer, 0x312a0219...). Plume is the canonical accounting/settlement hub. Per LayerZero's OVault Share mesh design, vault shares move via a ShareOFTAdapter (lockbox) on the hub chain plus standard ShareOFT mint/burn on spokes, with deposits/redemptions routed through the hub ERC-4626 vault (ABA pattern). This is an external LayerZero OFT-Adapter/lockbox route with a third-party control surface (composer + OFT peers), not a pure validated-network burn/mint, so it maps to external-lock-mint. The specific adapter contract and the named DVN set were not enumerated, hence probable rather than verified.

mintAuthority.summary: REUSD mint() requires operators[msg.sender] || msg.sender == owner(). No direct REUSD operators have been set, and owner() returns the Core contract (0xc07e…), Resupply's on-chain governance hub. Core.execute() is callable by the Voter contract (0x1111…), a token-weighted on-chain governance contract requiring quorum, a voting period, and execution delay; bounded Guardian operator permissions remain active for emergency actions but do not grant direct stablecoin mint access.

mintIncidents.summary: Resupply's crvUSD/wstUSR market exploit manipulated exchange-rate and solvency logic so negligible collateral could borrow up to the reUSD debt limit, leaving bad debt through the stablecoin borrow route.

controls.label: REUSD owner — Resupply Core governance contract
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25321527: owner() on REUSD returned 0xc07e000044f95655c11fda4cd37f70a94d7e0a7d. eth_getCode returned contract code. REUSD source: mint() requires operators[msg.sender] || msg.sender == owner(); no direct REUSD operator was found in the reviewed state. Core source: execute() is callable by voter 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6 (token-weighted on-chain governance) or operators with explicit per-selector permissions. Active GuardianUpgradeable permissions are bounded emergency/operator functions rather than direct stablecoin mint authority.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25321527: REUSD mint() is gated by owner (Core 0xc07e…) or direct stablecoin operators; Core.voter() returns 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6. The Voter contract enforces token-weighted proposal execution with 30% quorum, a 7-day voting period, and a 1-day execution delay. Resupply's docs state contracts are owned by Core and governed through on-chain voting. The current GuardianUpgradeable proxy is controlled by a 3-of-5 Safe and has bounded emergency/operator permissions, but the active implementation does not expose the older revertVoter path and does not hold direct REUSD mint authority. Mint authority is therefore DAO-governed with emergency multisig controls.

launchPhaseDetail: Selected as one of four firms for FCA Regulatory Sandbox stablecoin cohort (Feb 25); testing began Q1 2026; full UK banking licence granted Mar 11, but GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut Ltd (e-money entity), not Revolut Bank UK, per BoE proposed rule on subsidiary issuance; Head of UK Policy Rory Tanner outlined proposition to House of Lords (Mar 25), flagging UK→India remittance corridor as priority use case; ticker not publicly confirmed; the Bank of England softened its stance in May 2026 — dropping the £20k individual holding cap in favour of aggregate issuer caps (revised draft rules due June 2026) and signalling banks may issue branded coins via ring-fenced subsidiaries — though the 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement remains under review. On June 2 2026 the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee urged the BoE to scrap individual holding limits entirely and reconsider that 40% floor. On June 22 2026 the BoE published its final policy statement and draft rules: individual holding limits are scrapped in favour of a temporary per-coin issuance cap (initially ~£40bn / $50bn), the short-dated-UK-T-bill reserve share rises to 70% with the remainder held at the BoE and no yield paid to holders, and par redemption within 24 hours is required; a Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026, with rules finalised by end-2026 and regulated sterling stablecoins operating from 2027. UK full authorisation regime not active until October 2027

launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025 and operates an existing EMI licence in Lithuania — the legal foundations for issuing e-money tokens under MiCA Title IV. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot — though that sandbox is specifically for a GBP token, not USD. Revolut received a full UK banking licence from the PRA (Mar 11 2026) and filed an OCC national bank charter application for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Mar 5 2026, targeting a 2027 US launch with built-in stablecoin access). A Revolut-branded proprietary USD stablecoin has not been officially confirmed; the USD path runs through the Lithuanian EMI / MiCA EMT route, and Polymarket currently puts the probability at ~33% by year-end 2026. Specific ticker, chain selection, and reserve disclosure model remain unannounced.

name: Spiko Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund
oneLiner: SPKCC is the USD share class of Spiko's regulated French AIF combining a digital-asset cash-and-carry basis strategy with short-duration T-bill collateral.
collateral: USD share class of the Spiko Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund. Monthly allocation rotates between BTC and ETH cash-and-carry (basis) trades and short-duration Treasury bills/cash. Marex is the fund's sole strategy counterparty, spot digital assets are custodied at Coinbase, futures are cleared on CME, and CACEIS Bank (Credit Agricole Group) acts as depositary.
pegMechanism: USD-denominated NAV-accreting fund share; daily NAV is calculated by CACEIS Fund Administration and published on-chain through a Chainlink AggregatorV3-style oracle contract. Holdings are restricted to KYC-allowlisted addresses via Spiko's PermissionManager; minting is limited to the daily-operator role and burns to the Redemption contract's burner role.

jurisdiction.license: French Fonds Professionnel Specialise (FPS) / Alternative Investment Fund

mintAuthority.summary: SPKCC Ethereum mint/burn routes through Spiko's PermissionManager (ERC1967Proxy). Mint requires PermissionManager group 0 (ADMIN) or group 2 (daily-operator). Group 2 is a rotating Spiko EOA; group 0 ADMIN holder is not identifiable from on-chain state alone.

controls.label: SPKCC token (UUPS proxy, restricted mint/burn via PermissionManager)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295096, EIP-1967 impl slot = 0x15ea0ec460a0e6847ec0aa8d50a84b3a51b95f74 (Token.sol). Token authority() = PermissionManager proxy 0x344278aff. mint() requires restricted() → PermissionManager.canCall(msg.sender, token, mint_selector). getRequirements(token, mint) = groups {0, 2}.

controls.label: Spiko PermissionManager (ERC1967Proxy) — shared authority policy
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295096, ERC1967 impl = 0xd3f5f1524e1a472b51374a3ff41b8936eb5b658e (PermissionManager). Group structure: group 0 = ADMIN (controls everything), group 2 = daily-operator/minter, group 5 = KYC operator (manages group 6 user allowlist). Group 2 admins = group 0 only. getGroupAdmins(0) = {0} (self-referential). Group 0 holder not determinable from on-chain state.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295096: PermissionManager fully decoded — group 0 (ADMIN) controls mint authorization; group 2 (daily-operator) is the rotating EOA minter; minting at block 23169041 confirmed EOA 0x2B3755 in group 2. Group 0 ADMIN not found via getGroups() queries on known addresses; _permissions mapping not enumerable without brute force. Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Starknet, Stellar lanes not verified.
unresolvedQuestions: Identify and verify the PermissionManager group 0 (ADMIN) holder — the entity that controls minter group 2 membership — before promoting to verified.
Resolve Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Starknet, and Stellar mint or bridge authorities before claiming multichain completeness.

name: SoulPeg USD
oneLiner: spUSD is SoulPeg's freely tradable BNB Chain wrapper around a soul-bound sUSDC position routed through Venus lending; no Pharos-reviewed holder USDC exit.
collateral: USDC deposited via SoulPeg's mint flow on BNB Chain, automatically routed into Venus Protocol lending markets to generate yield; spUSD itself is a freely transferable ERC-20 wrapper around a soul-bound sUSDC position
pegMechanism: Two-token system: soul-bound sUSDC is minted 1:1 against USDC and accrues Venus lending yield for the original wallet; SPUSD (spUSD) is a 1:1 freely tradeable ERC-20 wrapper around sUSDC and is convertible 1:1 at the wrapper contract; Pharos has not source-reviewed a holder-exercisable USDC exit route for SPUSD, so no redemption backstop is modeled

mintAuthority.summary: spUSD is a role-gated BSC wrapper: the SoulPeg wrapper contract (0x0e8fb2e…) holds MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE on-chain; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by EOA 0xf683ab3…. MAX_SUPPLY is an immutable constant at 1B tokens.

applicabilityBasis.summary: sUSD is explicitly designed as a yield-bearing stablecoin that passes T-bill interest to holders via Solana Token-2022 interest extension. The GENIUS Act Section 4(a)(11) prohibits permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying any form of interest or yield to holders solely in connection with holding the stablecoin. Whether sUSD qualifies as a 'payment stablecoin' subject to this prohibition (and therefore potentially non-compliant as currently structured) or falls outside the payment-stablecoin definition as a yield-bearing investment instrument remains unresolved pending final GENIUS Act implementing regulations. No official guidance has classified yield-bearing RWA-backed stablecoins. Applicability is genuinely unclear.

genius.notes: Solayer Labs, Inc. is a US-incorporated company headquartered in San Francisco (CA corp, doc #6557004). sUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin backed by US Treasury bills via a partnership with OpenEden (Moody's-rated RWA platform). The yield is passed to holders through Solana Token-2022 interest extension mechanics — a design that sits in regulatory tension with the GENIUS Act's yield prohibition on payment stablecoin issuers. No GENIUS authorization, application, or registration found. No enforcement action found. The applicability question (payment stablecoin vs. excluded yield instrument) will only be resolved once final GENIUS implementing regulations are issued.

obituary.epitaph: Saved the protocol at the cost of its dollar
obituary.obituary: Launched in 2018, sUSD was Synthetix's flagship synthetic dollar — an overcollateralized stablecoin minted against staked SNX. Its peg held for years on a single reflex: whenever sUSD slipped below $1, stakers bought it back at a discount to repay their debt at par. SIP-420 (April 2025) dismantled that reflex, cutting the required collateral ratio from 750% to 200% and pooling debt collectively — minting got cheap, but no individual was left with a reason to defend the dollar. sUSD fell to $0.68 within weeks and never recovered, drifting below peg for over a year as supply bled from a ~$329M peak toward a functionally insolvent tail near $0.23. In June 2026 Synthetix governance stopped repairing it and passed SIP-423: the contract was frozen, a holder snapshot taken, and sUSD made permanently non-transferable, with remaining holders repaid in vested SNX on a 4:1 schedule.

genius.notes: Anchorage Digital Bank is an uninsured OCC-chartered national trust bank (the first federally chartered crypto bank, chartered January 2021). Under the GENIUS Act, this corresponds to the federal qualified payment stablecoin issuer (FQPSI) pathway supervised by the OCC. Anchorage has submitted a comment letter on the OCC NPRM and publicly states it expects to become a PPSI once the GENIUS Act framework takes effect (rules still in proposed-rulemaking stage as of 2026-06-18). No PPSI approval has been granted to any issuer. The OCC's proposed rule raises a potential 'one issuer, one brand' restriction that could affect Anchorage's white-label model (it currently issues USAT, USDtb/Ethena, USDGO/OSL, and a forthcoming USDPT/Western Union).

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USBD is a native LayerZero Omnichain Fungible Token (OFT): its verified Ethereum DebtToken source imports @layerzerolabs/oft-evm/contracts/OFT.sol and is declared `contract DebtToken is OFT`, taking a LayerZero V2 endpoint in its constructor (send/quoteSend/lzReceive/setPeer present), so supply moves via burn-on-source / mint-on-destination over LayerZero messaging — a regular OFT, not a lockbox adapter or a third-party liquidity bridge (the L2BEAT 'Across' reference is just a bridge that can route USBD, not its issuance path). The identical CREATE2 address across ethereum/hemi/plume/sonic/bsc/nibiru is the OFT pattern. Classified at external-lock-mint (40) rather than external-validated-network (65) because, while the OFT burn/mint mechanism is verified from primary contract source, the DVN security stack is neither named nor reviewed: LayerZeroScan was rate-limited and Bima publishes no LayerZero/OFT/DVN documentation, so this is a generic OFT with an unreviewed third-party control surface.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDe is a synthetic delta-neutral dollar with a nominal $1 redemption obligation but backed by crypto derivatives positions and liquid stablecoins rather than HQLA (cash, Fed balances, short-term Treasuries). The Act mandates a separate regulatory study on non-payment stablecoins, suggesting synthetic dollars occupy an unresolved category. Applicability is marked unclear pending that study and final rulemaking.

name: Noble Dollar
oneLiner: USDN is Noble chain's native rebasing yield-bearing dollar backed by short-term U.S. T-bills via M0, with T-bill yield accruing directly to USDN balances.
collateral: Short-term U.S. Treasury Bills held in bankruptcy-remote SPVs via M0 Protocol; over 100% collateral coverage maintained by M0 Minters (including Superstate and MXON); collateral verified daily on-chain
pegMechanism: Rebasing yield-bearing stablecoin; USDN is collateralized by M0's $M token on Ethereum via M0's Portal bridge (Wormhole NTT); the Noble chain module tracks each holder's principal against the latest rebasing multiplier from M0 on Ethereum, accruing T-bill yield directly to USDN balances; users mint/redeem via USDC through the Noble Express app

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing stablecoin that accrues T-bill yield directly to holder balances every 30 seconds via M0's rebase mechanism. The GENIUS Act defines a payment stablecoin as one the issuer is obligated to redeem at a fixed monetary value; USDN balances grow over time rather than redeeming at a fixed amount. The Act also explicitly prohibits payment stablecoin issuers from paying any yield to holders — USDN's entire design is yield distribution. These structural features place USDN outside the GENIUS payment stablecoin definition.

genius.notes: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing T-bill wrapper built on M0 infrastructure; it falls outside the GENIUS Act payment stablecoin definition because (1) it does not redeem at a fixed monetary value (balances rebase upward as yield accrues), and (2) its core design distributes yield directly to holders, which the Act prohibits for in-scope payment stablecoins. Noble's legal entity is NASD Inc (US-based); M0 provides infrastructure but is not the issuer. Noble announced migration from Cosmos appchain to EVM L1 in January 2026; USDN remains the flagship asset on the new chain.

references.label: GENIUS Act text S.1582 – payment stablecoin definition and yield prohibition

controls.label: MoC Governor / Changer governance
controls.evidence: RIF On Chain uses the Money on Chain Governor/Changer pattern: parameter changes and proxy upgrades are executed on-chain via changer contracts after community votes (e.g., V2.0 and V3 upgrades were governance-executed proxy upgrades).

review.evidence: At Rootstock block 8935202: USDRIF token 0x3a15461d governor() selector (0x0c340a24) returned Governor proxy 0x3b8853df65afbd94853e6d77ee0ab5590f41bb08 (confirmed as a contract). Governor proxy EIP-1967 admin = ProxyAdmin 0x1a1824f39d79937dcb80c9d9938ae77e431c2def; ProxyAdmin storage slot 0 (owner) = 0x131564703310a294c1bfdc09d10ec0659f18e253 (also a proxy with ProxyAdmin = 0x1a1824, circular). Governor proxy owner() = 0x65a5681be95d212f0c90ead40170d8277de81169 (proxy, impl = 0x00594d5456c4650d10edbb62d7a482d8fa9a5b53); calling governor() on 0x65a5681 returned 0x3b8853 (back to the Governor proxy). USDRIF token EIP-1967 implementation = 0x6d1bb87856a2b2351d87ba5772a93dc911325af9. The governance chain forms a RIF-On-Chain Foundation control set (same MoC BitVoting / Foundation architecture as DOC). Final controlling authority cannot be confirmed as a Safe or timelock on-chain — it terminates in a recursive proxy-of-proxies controlled by RIF Foundation keys.
unresolvedQuestions: The RIF On Chain Governor proxy control chain terminates in a recursive proxy set (0x65a5681 ↔ 0x3b8853 ↔ 0x131564 ↔ 0x1a1824); the final human-controlled authority (multisig threshold/keyholders) is not enumerable from on-chain state — characteristic of MoC Foundation BitVoting; Arbitrum bridge mint authority also unresolved.

controls.evidence: At BSC block 103620388: token owner() = 0x8e3811b4…; getOwners() returned 5 EOA addresses (all eth_getCode=0x), threshold()=3, getModulesPaginated returned empty array (no modules), guard slot 6 = 0x0 (no guard), VERSION()='1.4.1'. controls.label: USDU Solana mint authority
controls.evidence: Solana Token-2022 mint 9ckR7pPP…: mintAuthority = the mint address itself (self-referential). Extensions present: metadataPointer and tokenMetadata (updateAuthority also = mint address). No freezeAuthority. Supply = 10,951,433 USDU. This pattern cannot be verified via standard key-based authority reads — the controlling program or keypair is unknown from on-chain state alone. Judgment per the moveUSD precedent: a self-referential Token-2022 mintAuthority (the mint address itself) is a non-executable, non-signing account, so no party can invoke MintTo on Solana; the Solana supply is effectively frozen.

review.evidence: BSC block 103620388: Safe 3-of-5 (all EOA signers, no modules/guard, v1.4.1) confirmed as token owner with mint() = onlyOwner. Solana: Token-2022 mintAuthority = mint address itself (9ckR7pPP…), a self-referential configuration that cannot be verified as a standard keypair or program authority via on-chain reads. obituary.epitaph: When one key minted eighty million
obituary.obituary: On 22 March 2026, an attacker exploited Resolv's single-EOA minter — no oracle, no amount cap, no max-mint guard — depositing 100K USDC and receiving 50M USR in return, then iterating until 80M unbacked USR existed for ~$25M of extracted ETH. USR crashed to $0.025 in 17 minutes; the RLP insurance layer absorbed the bad debt and was wiped out, dragging Stream Finance's $17M position down with it. Resolv burned 46M of the unbacked supply via a blacklist freeze, but USR never recovered — by April it traded at $0.16 with $95M of collateral against $173M of liabilities. Delta-neutral collateral and Apostro-attested reserves were no defense against an operator-level privilege failure.

name: VNDC
oneLiner: VNDC is Jade Labs's VND-denominated token, now disclosed as VNDC 2.0 backed by USDT/USDC pools under issuer and investigation risk.
collateral: Issuer-disclosed VNDC 2.0 USDT/USDC smart-contract collateral on Polygon and BNB Smart Chain; reserve and redemption claims remain high-risk after the March 2026 ONUS/VNDC investigation

mintAuthority.summary: VNDC is issued by Jade Labs (Singapore) and operated through the ONUS/VNDC Hub platforms; minting and redemption run through an issuer-controlled, admin-gated token with no third-party audit and no permissionless mint route.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: VNDC is issued natively and independently on each chain by Jade Labs via owner/whitelist-controlled mint and redeem - the Ethereum contract (VNDCToken, Solidity 0.4.11) uses owner issue()/burn(), and the BSC and Polygon contracts (both TokenVNDC, Solidity 0.8.18, byte-identical source) use mintWhitelist()/withdrawWhitelist(). None of the three deployments contain any OFT, LayerZero/CCIP/Wormhole/Axelar/Hyperlane messaging, lockbox, or bridge interface, and the addresses differ per chain (ruling out a deterministic-CREATE2 omnichain standard). The Polygon deployment is independent issuer mint, not a Polygon PoS bridge-minted token (no deposit/childChainManager/DEPOSITOR_ROLE). Cross-network movement is handled off-chain through the ONUS/VNDC Hub app (redeem on source, reissue on destination), with no autonomous on-chain bridge carrying the durable supply, so this is native multichain issuance rather than an opaque bridge route.

notices.title: Vietnam criminal investigation and withdrawal freeze
notices.message: Vietnamese authorities arrested ONUS/VNDC-linked executives in March 2026 in a fraud and money-laundering investigation involving VNDC, ONUS, and related tokens. Local reporting also described platform withdrawal disruptions during the investigation, so VNDC redemption and reserve claims should be treated as high risk.

notices.title: Market cap and supply inconsistency
notices.message: Aggregator-reported market cap (~$50M) does not consistently match on-chain Polygon/BSC supply, and reserves are self-disclosed by Jade Labs without an independent audit cadence.

notices.title: Curated reserves are self-reported
notices.message: The curated-validated live-reserves adapter points at the Jade Labs / VNDC issuer website because no third-party attestation page has been verified. Reserve composition reflects the issuer's own disclosure only until an independent auditor or proof-of-reserves feed is published.

name: Virtue USD
oneLiner: VUSD is Virtue Money's CDP dollar on IOTA, minted by borrowing against overcollateralized IOTA and stIOTA positions with liquidation defending the peg.
collateral: Overcollateralized IOTA, stIOTA, and IBTC (bridged BTC) positions backing VUSD debt inside the Virtue Money protocol
pegMechanism: CDP-style mint: users borrow VUSD against IOTA or stIOTA collateral and repay debt to unlock collateral, with liquidation and redemption mechanics supporting the U.S. dollar peg

mintAuthority.summary: VUSD is on IOTA Rebased (Move VM). The package at 0xd3b63e...904f is immutable, but contains an admin module. An AdminCap object (0x38a7b38d...) is held by EOA/address 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12. AdminCap gates set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, and set_beneficiary — active admin privileges over mint supply.

controls.label: Virtue Money borrower-operations / branch contracts (Liquity V2 fork)
controls.capDescription: Mint bounded by overcollateralized CDPs across IOTA/stIOTA branches with user-set interest rates, per the Liquity V2 multi-collateral design.
controls.evidence: Virtue docs describe VUSD as minted by opening overcollateralized CDPs using IOTA/stIOTA on a Liquity V2 friendly fork on IOTA EVM with user-set rates, flash minting, and liquidation/redemption peg defense.

controls.label: Virtue Money AdminCap holder
controls.evidence: At IOTA Rebased (confirmed via iota_getObject): AdminCap object 0x38a7b38d0f03338397d1c57f2cc2e3d7c5e3f6fe6887626aacc4cb4e8072c3f5 is owned by AddressOwner 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (version 591278735). Package 0xd3b63e...904f is Immutable (no upgrade). The admin module exposes no public entry functions but AdminCap gates vusd::set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, and set_beneficiary. Whether this address is a single EOA or a multisig could not be determined on-chain.

review.evidence: IOTA Rebased GraphQL confirmed AdminCap (type 0xd3b63e...::admin::AdminCap) is held by address 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (AddressOwner). iota_getNormalizedMoveModulesByPackage revealed vusd module exposing set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, set_beneficiary — all AdminCap-gated. Package owner type = Immutable (cannot be re-published). The AdminCap holder address owns no other enumerable objects, so it may be a multisig or single-keypair; cannot confirm threshold/type from chain state alone. Promotion judgment: the AdminCap holder address is confirmed on-chain; on Move-VM chains an address holder is EOA-equivalent (single-key vs k-of-n keypair custody is indistinguishable from chain state, matching the EVM EOA custody rule and the standard applied to BUCK and suiUSDe on Sui). All mint-capable surfaces (immutable branch contracts; parameter-only AdminCap) are confirmed.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Virtue is a crypto-collateralized protocol, but the IOTA deployment is not yet represented in Pharos contract metadata and available sources do not prove the absence of admin or pause surfaces.

oracleRisk.summary: Public docs reviewed for Virtue USD do not identify the collateral oracle setup or failure handling.

applicabilityBasis.summary: WEMIX Dollar (WEMIX$) is a USD-pegged, fiat-backed stablecoin issued by WEMIX PTE. LTD. (Singapore) under a permissioned mint-and-redemption model collateralized by USDC and fiat reserves. It circulated as the native settlement currency of the WEMIX3.0 gaming blockchain and was accessible to US-person users via international exchanges, matching the GENIUS Act definition of a payment stablecoin. The issuer announced a wind-down and transition to USDC.e in 2025; circulating supply has declined significantly but remains non-zero as of mid-2026 (CoinGecko reports approximately 14.5M WEMIX$ in circulation). Applicability is assessed on the basis of the token's design and issuance during its active life.

genius.notes: WEMIX PTE. LTD. (UEN 201903432D, formerly WEMADE TREE PTE. LTD.) is a Singapore-incorporated subsidiary of South Korean game developer WEMADE. The issuer announced in 2025 that WEMIX$ would be wound down and replaced by USDC.e (Circle bridged USDC via Chainlink CCIP). As of June 2026, CoinGecko (the coin's configured detailProvider) reports approximately 14.5M WEMIX$ still in circulation with minimal trading activity (~$33/day volume on WEMIX.Fi), indicating the wind-down is substantially advanced but not yet complete. No GENIUS Act PPSI application, foreign-issuer registration, or authorization announcement has been located. The foreign exception status is not-applicable because the GENIUS Act's foreign-issuer registration framework (Treasury comparability rule) remains in proposed-rules phase as of June 2026 and no determinations have been made. The issuer has made no public announcement of intent to engage with the GENIUS framework.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: WEUSD moves cross-chain via PicWe's own issuer-operated burn-on-source / mint-on-destination route. PicWe's cross-chain-transfer docs state "Source chain burns, target chain mints" over a self-built native bridge ("No Wormhole. No LayerZero. No third-party risk") with PicWe-operated keepers signing and verifying every cross-chain message. On-chain this is confirmed: the EVM token (identical CREATE2 address 0xdd73... on bsc/base/arbitrum/plume) is a plain ERC20 + AccessControl with no LayerZero/Wormhole/OFT interface, so cross-chain mints flow purely through MINTER_ROLE held by a PicWe admin EOA plus the mint/redeem contract, and on Movement through the weusd_cross_chain_gas cross_mint_role_contract relayer (batchMintWeUSDCrossChain). The durable supply path is therefore issuer-native burn/mint, not an external validated network, canonical bridge, or liquidity route. Trust posture is weak: keeper validation has no published external attestation or audit, control keys are concentrated PicWe EOAs with no multisig/timelock, and the token trades off-peg (~$0.91) under disputed backing.

applicabilityBasis.summary: WTGXX is a share class of a Rule 2a-7-registered Investment Company Act of 1940 money market fund (WisdomTree Treasury Money Market Digital Fund), making it a security under federal securities laws. The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, signed July 18, 2025) explicitly excludes from the payment stablecoin definition any digital asset that is a security as defined in section 2 of the Securities Act of 1933, section 3 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, or section 2 of the Investment Company Act of 1940. WTGXX is not marketed as a payment instrument — it is positioned as a qualifying GENIUS Act reserve asset for payment stablecoin issuers, not as a payment stablecoin itself.

name: Zephyr Stable Dollar
oneLiner: ZSD is Zephyr Protocol's dollar stablecoin on a Monero-derived private chain, minted from ZEPH base-coin collateral through a Djed-inspired reserve mechanism.
collateral: ZEPH base-coin collateral held by the Zephyr Protocol reserve; the protocol targets overcollateralization before allowing new ZSD minting
pegMechanism: Users mint or redeem ZSD against ZEPH through Zephyr's Djed-inspired reserve mechanism, with oracle pricing and reserve-ratio constraints maintaining the dollar target

mintAuthority.summary: ZSD is minted and redeemed through Zephyr's native reserve-ratio protocol rules against ZEPH collateral. Source code review confirms no admin/emergency mint path: all transaction_type enum values (MINT_STABLE, MINT_RESERVE, MINT_YIELD) are user-facing; blockchain.cpp contains no admin override. The Zephyr foundation controls the oracle RSA signing key (cryptonote_config.h), a price-feed centralization vector, but not a privileged mint bypass.

controls.label: Zephyr native reserve mint/redeem rules
controls.capDescription: Minting depends on native reserve-ratio and oracle rules in protocol consensus; no EVM-style privileged minter exists.
controls.evidence: Source review of enums.h confirmed transaction_type enum lists only user-facing types (MINT_STABLE, REDEEM_STABLE, MINT_RESERVE, REDEEM_RESERVE, MINT_YIELD, REDEEM_YIELD, TRANSFER variants, AUDIT types) — no ADMIN_MINT or emergency bypass type. blockchain.cpp contains no 'admin', 'foundation', 'emergency', or 'bypass' patterns. cryptonote_config.h includes a hardcoded foundation oracle RSA key (ORACLE_PUBLIC_KEY), which controls price-feed signing but is not a direct mint authority.

review.evidence: Source code reviewed 2026-06-11. No admin/emergency/foundation mint bypass found in enums.h, blockchain.cpp, or cryptonote_tx_utils.cpp. All mint paths are reserve-ratio-gated user transactions. Foundation holds oracle signing key (price-feed centralization) but not a privileged minter role.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Zephyr documentation presents ZSD as a native asset on a Monero-derived protocol and does not identify an issuer-controlled freeze, blacklist, pause, privileged burn, or proxy-upgrade control surface for holder balances.

oracleRisk.summary: Public Zephyr docs mention a pricing oracle for ZSD but do not identify the oracle provider set or failure handling.

notices.title: Unsupported private chain
notices.message: ZSD primarily circulates as a native Zephyr asset on a Monero-derived chain, which is not a configured Pharos chain, so no contract is stored.
